question.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{yz})-\sqrt{x+1},$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=0.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{yz})-\sqrt{x+1} & =0 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{yz}) & =\sqrt{x+1} \\ \sqrt{yz} & ={e}^{\sqrt{x+1}} \\ yz & ={({e}^{\sqrt{x+1}})}^{2} \\ z & =\frac{{e}^{2\sqrt{x+1}}}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface for $c=0$ is the surface $z=\frac{{e}^{2\sqrt{x+1}}}{y}.$
